items.followUp: A force has components Fₓ = 5 N and Fᵧ = 12 N. Find its magnitude and direction relative to the x-axis.

rubric.why: The magnitude follows from combining the perpendicular components.
rubric.description: Correct magnitude of the resultant force.

rubric.why: The direction is determined from tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ.
rubric.description: Correct direction relative to the positive x-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 36.9° above the x-axis, or an equivalent angle calculation.

items.followUp: Write the equation for kinetic energy. What happens to kinetic energy if the speed of a body is tripled?

rubric.why: This is the standard equation for kinetic energy.
Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the kinetic energy becomes four times its original value.

modelAnswer: Since K.E. ∝ v², if velocity becomes 2v, K.E. becomes ½m(2v)² = 4(½mv²).
Therefore, the kinetic energy becomes four times its original value.

items.followUp: A force of 50 N moves a body 20 m in the direction of the force. Find the work done.

rubric.why: Work is the product of force and displacement when they are in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for W = Fd and 1 mark for 30,000 J.

items.followUp: Write down any two non-renewable energy sources.

rubric.why: Renewable energy comes from sources that are naturally replenished.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

rubric.why: A second valid example completes the response.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different correct example.

modelAnswer: Two renewable energy sources are solar energy and wind energy.

items.followUp: Convert 86 °F into degrees Celsius and kelvin.

rubric.why: Kelvin temperature is obtained by adding 273 to the Celsius temperature.

items.followUp: What is internal energy? State one factor on which it depends.

rubric.why: Internal energy is the sum of the microscopic kinetic and potential energies of a body's molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the total kinetic and potential energy of the molecules.

rubric.why: These factors affect the energy of the molecules in a body.
rubric.description: A correct factor affecting internal energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one relevant factor, such as temperature or the amount of substance.

modelAnswer: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of its molecules.
It depends on factors such as the temperature, amount of substance, and nature and state of the substance.

items.followUp: Suggest four ways to reduce energy consumption in a school building.

rubric.why: Turning off unused devices avoids unnecessary energy use.
rubric.description: Switch off or unplug unused electrical devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable measure that prevents devices being left on unnecessarily.

rubric.why: Efficient equipment provides the same service using less energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for recommending efficient appliances, LED bulbs, or equivalent.

rubric.why: Insulation reduces heat transfer and the energy needed for heating or cooling.
rubric.description: Insulate the building to reduce heat loss or gain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate insulation measure.

rubric.why: Using sunlight or solar energy reduces reliance on other energy sources.
rubric.description: Make use of natural light or solar energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable use of sunlight or solar technology.

modelAnswer: Switch off lights, fans, and other appliances when they are not in use.
Use energy-efficient appliances and LED bulbs.
Insulate roofs and walls to reduce heat loss or gain.
Use daylight and install solar panels or solar water heaters where possible.

items.followUp: A square surface has sides of 5 mm. Find the pressure exerted on it by a force of 10 N.

rubric.why: The side length must be converted from millimetres to metres before calculating area in SI units.
rubric.description: Correct conversion of side length to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting 10 mm to 0.01 m.

rubric.why: The square's area is side × side.
rubric.description: Correct area of the square surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for A = (0.01 m)² = 0.0001 m².

rubric.why: Pressure equals force divided by area; the result is in pascals.
rubric.description: Correct pressure calculation and final answer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for P = F/A, 1 mark for correct substitution with SI units, and 1 mark for 2 × 10⁵ Pa.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N, side = 10 mm = 0.01 m
